addTheseParametersAndStartHere: Turn on Advanced Lateral Tune before trying any suggested profile.
This route looks broadly wrong enough that the first move should be a baseline fix, not a surgical cleanup pass.
Start with the broad knobs this report suggests. Once the car is in the right zip code, re-run analysis and switch to Cleanup Pass for the leftovers.
Generic advanced lateral params are in play on this pass, so apply those first before deciding you need deeper code-level changes.
Friction-threshold changes are active in this pass because the logs point to small-signal steering behavior, not just whole-tune authority.

suggestions.driverFeel: The car is doing repeated micro-corrections around center in the mid speed band while the requested path stays calm.
suggestions.ifThatWasWrong: If chatter remains after this threshold pass, re-analyze the next drive. FLM will move to a bounded deadband cleanup for the same speed band rather than repeatedly raising the whole threshold curve.
suggestions.likelyInterpretation: This looks more like a friction-threshold problem than a whole-tune problem; the controller is busy around center and needs a calmer deadzone slope.
suggestions.logSupport: Matched in 1470 event(s); strongest samples: 00000101--2f56dfdd5a/10, 00000101--2f56dfdd5a/10, 00000101--2f56dfdd5a/10. Strongest window: steering moved 0.83 deg peak-to-peak with 12 steering reversal(s) and 18 output reversal(s), while the desired path moved only 0.061 m/s^2 peak-to-peak
suggestions.observedBehavior: The car is doing repeated micro-corrections around center in the mid speed band while the requested path stays calm.
